steps.title: Prepare ethanol solution
steps.instruction: Mix 700 mL absolute ethanol (Fisher catalog 10048291) with 300 mL Milli‑Q water to obtain 1 L of 70 % (v/v) ethanol solution.

steps.title: Prepare deuterated phosphate buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 2.885 g Na₂HPO₄, 595 mg KH₂PO₄ and 3.45 mg TSP (Sigma‑Aldrich catalog 269913) in 100 mL D₂O (Sigma‑Aldrich catalog 151882); adjust pH to 7.0 with 5 M HCl.

steps.title: Size‑fractionate photogranules
steps.instruction: Sort oxygenic photogranules (OPGs) through 0.6 mm and 1.0 mm mesh sieves.

steps.title: Aliquot biomass into tubes
steps.instruction: Place 50 small OPGs (≈6 mg dry biomass) into each 2 mL screw‑cap tube containing 500 µL tap water. Optionally test a biomass gradient and use ≥8 replicates per condition.

steps.title: Pre‑store lysing matrix
steps.instruction: Store tubes of Lysing Matrix E (MP Biomedicals catalog 1169140‑CF; contains 1.4 mm ceramic spheres, 0.1 mm silica spheres and one 4 mm glass bead) at –80 °C for at least 24 h before sampling.

steps.title: Freeze harvested biomass
steps.instruction: Immediately after sampling, plunge the tubes with OPGs into liquid nitrogen; keep the biomass settled at the tube bottom. If extraction is delayed, store tubes at –80 °C (max 12 months).

steps.title: Add lysing beads to frozen samples
steps.instruction: On dry ice, open each frozen tube, discard the original cap, add the pre‑chilled Lysing Matrix E, and reseal with the matrix‑tube caps.

substeps.instruction: a. Remove Lysing Matrix E from –80 °C and keep on dry ice.
b. Transfer frozen sample tubes to a dry‑ice‑filled cryo‑box.
c. Open sample tubes, discard caps.
d. Add the cooled Lysing Matrix E to each tube.
e. Close tubes with the matrix caps.

steps.title: Add buffer RLT on ice
steps.instruction: Place tubes on an ice bed and add 600 µL Buffer RLT (from RNeasy Mini kit, Qiagen catalog 74104) to each tube.

steps.title: Mechanical lysis – first cycle
steps.instruction: Grind the tubes in a FastPrep instrument for 20 s at 6 m s⁻¹.

steps.title: Cool between grinding cycles
steps.instruction: Return tubes to the ice bed for 1 min.

steps.title: Mechanical lysis – second cycle
steps.instruction: Repeat the 20 s FastPrep grinding at 6 m s⁻¹; if lysis appears insufficient (e.g., no green supernatant), add additional cycles with 1 min ice cooling between cycles.

steps.title: Clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge tubes at 16,000 × g for 2 min at room temperature; keep the supernatant.

steps.title: Pass lysate through QIAshredder
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a QIAshredder spin column (Qiagen catalog 79654) at room temperature and centrifuge 16,000 × g for 2 min to remove beads and debris.

steps.title: Split eluate for downstream work
steps.instruction: Collect 300 µL of the flow‑through for RNA extraction (step E) and retain the remaining ≈450 µL for metabolite extraction (step C). The total volume must stay below the QIAshredder capacity (<750 µL).

steps.title: Add methanol to metabolite fraction
steps.instruction: To the ≈450 µL metabolite eluate, add 400 µL methanol (Fisher catalog 10499560) in a fume hood and vortex for 2 min with a multivortex.

steps.title: Add dichloromethane – first addition
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL dichloromethane (Fisher catalog 10626642) and vortex for 2 min (fume hood).

steps.title: Additional vortex and second dichloromethane
steps.instruction: Vortex the mixture for another 2 min, then add a second 200 µL of dichloromethane and vortex for 2 min (all steps in a fume hood).

steps.title: Phase separation on ice
steps.instruction: Place the tube on ice for 15 min at 4 °C to allow aqueous and organic phases to separate.

steps.title: Centrifuge for phase clarity
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 2,200 × g for 15 min at 4 °C in a refrigerated centrifuge.

steps.title: Collect aqueous and organic phases
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, collect 700 µL of the upper aqueous phase and 200 µL of the lower organic phase (the organic layer is ≈400 µL; only 200 µL is taken to avoid contamination).

steps.title: Short‑term storage before evaporation
steps.instruction: Store both phases at –80 °C (maximum 3 months) until evaporation.

steps.title: Evaporate aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Thaw the aqueous sample, then evaporate with a SpeedVac (no temperature, manual program, ramp 3). If the volume exceeds half the tube, split into two tubes: first evaporate 400 µL, store the residual solid at 4 °C, then evaporate the remaining 300 µL. Store the dried residue at –80 °C (max 3 months).

steps.title: Evaporate organic phase
steps.instruction: Under a fume hood, evaporate the organic phase under a gentle nitrogen stream at room temperature for at least 2 h; proceed directly to NMR tube loading once dry.

steps.title: Prepare aqueous NMR samples
steps.instruction: Re‑dissolve each dried aqueous residue in 270 µL deuterated phosphate buffer (Recipe 2), vortex (or use Tecan robot), centrifuge at 1,200 × g for 15 min at 4 °C, pool 25 µL from each sample for QC, transfer 200 µL into 3 mm NMR tubes, and fill the tube openings with beads (or cap).

substeps.instruction: a. Add 270 µL deuterated buffer to dry sample.
b. Mix with needles (robot) or vortex (manual).
d. Pool 25 µL aliquots for quality control.
e. Transfer 200 µL to 3 mm NMR tube.
f. Insert beads (or cap) to close tube.

steps.title: Prepare organic NMR samples
steps.instruction: Make a 2:1 (v/v) mixture of deuterated chloroform‑d (Sigma‑Aldrich catalog 343803) with 0.03 % TMS and deuterated methanol‑d (Sigma‑Aldrich catalog 151947); add 270 µL of this solution to each dried organic residue, take 25 µL for QC, transfer 200 µL into 3 mm NMR tubes, and seal with cap‑sealing balls (or caps).

substeps.instruction: a. Prepare 2:1 deuterated chloroform‑d/MeOD solution with 0.03 % TMS.
b. Add 270 µL to each sample with a Pasteur pipette.
c. Pipette 25 µL for quality‑control tube.
d. Transfer 200 µL to 3 mm NMR tube.
e. Insert cap‑sealing balls (or cap) to close tube.

steps.title: RNA extraction – ethanol precipitation
steps.instruction: Combine the 300 µL RNA eluate (step B) with 300 µL 70 % ethanol, mix by pipetting, and load ≈600 µL onto an RNeasy spin column (Qiagen catalog 74104) kept at room temperature.

steps.title: RNA extraction – column washes
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at max speed (~16,000 × g) for 1 min; discard flow‑through. Add 700 µL RW1 buffer, centrifuge 1 min, discard. Add 700 µL RPE buffer, centrifuge 1 min, discard. Add 500 µL RPE buffer, centrifuge 1 min, discard. Then centrifuge 2 min at max speed to remove residual RPE.

steps.title: RNA elution and cleanup
steps.instruction: Place the column in a new tube, add 35 µL RNase‑free water to the column center, centrifuge 2 min at max speed, collect eluate, re‑apply the eluate to the same column, centrifuge 2 min again. Keep a 5 µL aliquot for QC (Nanodrop/Qubit/BioAnalyzer) and store the remaining RNA at –20 °C.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol was tested on a set of 200 samples, demonstrating its robustness and reproducibility, obtaining sufficient concentrations of metabolites and RNA for subsequent metabolomic and metatranscriptomic analyses, while complying with the quality criteria for NMR spectra and RNA. A. NMR analysis In NMR, the standardized requirement for the limit of detection (LOD) and quantification (LOQ) are signal-to-noise ratios of ≥ 3 and 10, respectively [18]. In our case, most of the NMR spectra obtained had enough signals with a signal-to-noise ratio higher than 10. In the aqueous phase, on average, 120 peaks were detected per sample, and 12 ± 4 metabolites were identified per sample using the ASICS package (55 different metabolites were identified in the aqueous phase depending on the condition). The citrate signal at 2.67 ppm, coming from the RLT buffer and displayed in Figure 3 , masked some information and is certainly responsible for the relatively small number of metabolites identified here (see General Note 1). In the organic phase, around 150 peaks were detected per sample, and 17 ± 4 metabolites were identified per sample (altogether 88 different metabolites were identified in the organic phase depending on the condition). Raw NMR spectra can be found in the following database: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14383486. Figure 3. 1 H NMR spectra of photogranules metabolome. A. 1 H NMR spectra of the lipidic phase in CDCl 3 /CD 3 OD (2/1). B. 1 H NMR spectra of the aqueous phase in D 2 O. The quality of the analysis was controlled at multiple points for both phases to ensure that there was no drift or other introductions of errors in the results. For this, dedicated control samples (a pool of all samples, corresponding to quality controls) were analyzed repeatedly after a series of ten unknown samples.
